desk.headline: HEPS down 6.8% to 272.8c on weak UK and Australia; TFG Africa grows; interim dividend cut to 121c; no figures given for H2
results: Headline earnings per share fell 6.8% to 272.8c; revenue was flat at R31.4bn and retail turnover slipped 0.4% to R29bn.
TFG Africa, about two-thirds of sales, grew turnover 3.8% to R19.7bn and operating profit 2.7% to R1.7bn, helped by online sales up 53% to R2.2bn.
TFG London turnover fell 2.2% and TFG Australia 4.4% in local currency, with operating profit down 26.5% and 28.3% respectively.
The group closed 178 stores and opened 71; cash from operations rose 20% to R3.7bn, capex fell 37% to R672m and net debt dropped to R9.1bn.
The interim dividend was cut to 121c from 130c.

guidance.summary: TFG gives no profit or sales targets. It expects higher fuel prices and interest rates to keep shoppers under pressure, plans 60–80 more store closures in Africa and expects about R222m more cost savings in the second half.

points: CEO Anthony Thunström said TFG Africa grew sales, profit and market share in a tough six months.
He said over 95% of staff affected by store closures were moved to other roles.
Management stressed the cost programme, a smaller store base and the Bash online platform as the drivers to watch over the next 12–24 months.
Trading after the half was weaker: TFG Africa sales fell 0.7% and Australia 5.3% in the five weeks to end-October.
An October cyber incident hit Phase Eight, Hobbs and Whistles in the UK, with own-website demand down about 30%.
call.source: Business Day (9 Nov 2026), Bizcommunity (6 Nov 2026) and Business News Today (9 Nov 2026) coverage of the results
